canonical_statement: The study compared clinical outcomes of cefadroxil oral transitional therapy with intravenous-only and alternative oral therapy for susceptible Gram-positive bacteremia, including cases with nonvertebral osteomyelitis.
This was a multicenter retrospective cohort study across four Los Angeles County Department of Health Services hospitals from September 1, 2022 through April 30, 2025.
The final analytic cohort contained 323 bacteremia episodes: 58 cefadroxil, 72 intravenous-only, and 193 alternative oral therapy episodes.

canonical_statement: The retrospective observational design leaves the study susceptible to unmeasured confounding and selection bias.

Baseline imbalances and hospital-specific treatment patterns could have influenced comparisons, including higher SSTI prevalence in the cefadroxil cohort and greater S. aureus prevalence in the IV cohort.
Because endocarditis, vertebral osteomyelitis, prosthetic infections, and central nervous system infections were excluded, findings should not be extrapolated to those high-risk syndromes.
Both oral-therapy groups received a median of 5 inpatient IV days, so the study does not establish the effectiveness of an earlier oral switch.

The authors concluded that cefadroxil transitional therapy had similar treatment success, mortality, and recurrence to IV and alternative oral antibiotics in selected lower-risk MSSA and streptococcal bacteremia and was well tolerated.
No funding was required for the study.
The authors reported no potential conflicts of interest.
The study datasets are available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.
